# Selesnya Rabbits

- **Format:** Casual 60-card, 1v1
- **Archetype:** Selesnya go-wide tokens: flood the board with Rabbits and 1/1 tokens, then win with one big pumped alpha strike (Overrun, Rabbit Response, Warren Elder)
- **Played by:** either — suits whoever enjoyed the Bloomburrow Hare Raising kit and likes big, dramatic attack turns
- **Status:** idea
- **Paired against:** [Orzhov Vampires](orzhov-vampires.md)
- **Complexity:** 2/5
- **Estimated power:** 5.5 with owned cards only, 6.5 with the buys (on a 1v1 scale)
- **Configuration:** Pair 3. It uses no precon cards, so its cards have all arrived and it can be built now, alongside Izzet and Gruul. It's in the **Commander-season** set too (with Giada, Gisa, Izzet and Gruul), where it takes over from Angels vs Zombies once the precons go back to being Commander decks.

A green-white 'go-wide' deck built on the Bloomburrow Hare Raising kit you already know. It floods the table with Rabbits, Cats, Dogs and 1/1 tokens, then wins in one big attack pumped by Overrun, Rabbit Response or Warren Elder. It is the faster deck of the pair and mostly about combat maths. It has no life-gain engine (the only life it gains is incidental: Blossoming Sands, Carrot Cake and Regal Caracal's lifelink Cats), and its removal comes from its own creatures (Bite Down, Rabid Bite, Felling Blow) plus Broken Wings for flyers. Great for whoever likes building up to one dramatic turn.

### Why these buys (in priority order)

1. **3x Valley Questcaller** (replaces 2 Savannah Lions + 1 Dryad Militant). Rabbit lord: every other Rabbit, including the Hop to It and Carrot Cake tokens, gets +1/+1, and you scry 1 whenever Rabbits enter. The biggest single upgrade: about +2 pts for the first copy and +3.5 for two in the simulator. *Also useful in: Finneas, Ace Archer Commander deck (a core buy there); any Rabbit/Bird/Bat deck.*
2. **2x Sunpetal Grove** (replaces Temple of Plenty + Selesnya Guildgate). G/W land that enters untapped once you have a Forest or Plains. Faster turns 1–3 and an easier GGG for Overrun. About +3 pts for the pair. *Also useful in: Finneas Commander deck; any G/W deck.*
3. **1x Burrowguard Mentor** (replaces Resolute Reinforcements). 3rd copy of the deck's best 2-drop: a trampler as big as your creature count. About +3 pts in the simulator. *Also useful in: any G/W tokens deck. The Finneas list also runs 1, so a 4th copy is needed if both decks are built (see the Finneas deck's Tier 2, section B).*
4. **2x Harvestrite Host** (replaces 1 Helpful Hunter + Dawnwing Marshal). 3-mana 3/3 Rabbit. Whenever it or another Rabbit enters, one of your creatures gets +1/+0 until end of turn, and the second time that ability resolves in a turn you draw a card. Hop to It alone does it (three Rabbits enter, so it triggers three times); so does a Carrot Cake token plus another Rabbit. Gives card flow and a real body. *Also useful in: Finneas Commander deck (core buy).*
5. **1x Hop to It** (replaces Crusader of Odric). 3rd copy of the best token maker (three 1/1 Rabbits for 3 mana), boosted by Questcaller and Host. *Also useful in: Finneas Commander deck.*

## Substitutes

| Target-list buy | Owned card played until it arrives | What the swap costs |
|---|---|---|
| Valley Questcaller ×3 | Savannah Lions ×2, Dryad Militant | The biggest loss. With no Rabbit lord, tokens stay 1/1 and you get no scry to smooth draws. About −3 pts head-to-head |
| Sunpetal Grove ×2 | Temple of Plenty, Selesnya Guildgate | Two more tapped lands slow turns 1–3 and make Overrun's GGG harder. About −3 pts |
| Burrowguard Mentor (3rd) | Resolute Reinforcements | Small. Reinforcements still gives 2 bodies at instant speed, but no big trampler. About −2 pts |
| Harvestrite Host ×2 | Helpful Hunter (2nd), Dawnwing Marshal | Small. Hunter draws a card and Marshal flies and pumps the team, but Host is a bigger body with repeatable card draw |
| Hop to It (3rd) | Crusader of Odric | Very small. Crusader is also a go-wide payoff |

Together the owned list is about 9–10 pts weaker than the target list against the same opponent. That's why the buys should arrive together with the Vampires' buys.

## Notes

### Game plan
- **Turns 1–3:** put as many bodies on the table as you can: cheap creatures (Warren Elder, Burrowguard Mentor, Finneas; plus Savannah Lions in the owned list and Valley Questcaller in the target list) and token makers (Carrot Cake, Hop to It, Prideful Parent; plus Resolute Reinforcements in the owned list). A *token* is a creature made by another card. It fights like any other creature.
- **Turns 4–5:** make the team bigger. Wilt-Leaf Liege is an *anthem* (a card that pumps all your creatures). Also Druid of the Spade, Treeguard Duo, Regal Caracal and Release the Dogs.
- **Then one big alpha strike** (attacking with everything at once) with Overrun, Rabbit Response or Warren Elder's pump. Until then, only attack with creatures that won't simply die to a blocker.
- **Removal:** Bite Down, Rabid Bite and Felling Blow make your biggest creature deal its damage to one of theirs, and it doesn't get hit back. Broken Wings kills a flyer. Bite Down and Broken Wings are instants; Rabid Bite and Felling Blow are sorceries. If they kill your creature in response, a bite spell does nothing, so bite when they have no mana open.

### Opening hand and mulligan
- **Keep:** 2–4 lands with at least two cards you can cast by turn 3, ideally with both a green and a white source.
- **Mulligan** (shuffle, draw a new 7, then put 1 card on the bottom for each mulligan you've taken): 0–1 lands, 6–7 lands, or a hand where everything costs 4 or more.
- On the draw (going second), a 2-land hand with three 2-drops is fine.

### Play tips
1. **Count before you Overrun.** All your creatures get +3/+3 and *trample* (damage beyond what kills a blocker goes through to the player). Add up what your attackers will deal. If it beats their life, go. If not, build one more turn.
2. **Rabbit Response is an instant.** Cast it after they've chosen blockers: +2/+1 turns many of their 'safe' blocks into losses and makes unblocked creatures hit harder. You also get *scry 2* (look at your top two cards and keep or bottom each) because you control a Rabbit.
3. **Druid of the Spade is only a 2/3 without a token.** Play a token maker first when you can; then it's a 4/3 trampler.
4. **Warren Elder:** spend spare mana on {3}{W} during your attack to give everyone +1/+1. You can activate it more than once.
5. **Kill Marauding Blight-Priest on sight.** Save Broken Wings for Vampire Nighthawk, Dazzling Angel, Bloodtithe Collector or Inspiring Overseer.
6. **Byrke:** whenever a creature with a +1/+1 counter attacks, its counters double. Counters from Byrke's own entry, Felling Blow and earlier Finneas attacks all count.

### Watch out for (Vampires)
- **Marauding Blight-Priest:** every time they gain life, you lose 1. Their deck gains life constantly (Hinterland Sanctifier, Dazzling Angel, lifelink).
- **Ajani's Pridemate, Fiendish Panda, Twinblade Paladin** grow with every life gain. Deal with them before they're 6/6.
- **Vengeful Bloodwitch:** each of their creatures that dies drains you 1, so blocks and trades cost you life.
- **Instant removal** (Go for the Throat, Hero's Downfall, Mortify, Moment of Craving) can kill a creature in the middle of your attack. Don't rely on one big creature.
- **Exsanguinate:** they pay X plus 2 mana to drain X. With 7 lands that's 5 life, so leave a margin when racing.
- **Deathtouch blockers** (Ayli and Vampire Nighthawk; in their target list also Vampire of the Dire Moon and Gifted Aetherborn) kill anything they block. Attack wide with small creatures rather than sending one big one in, or kill them first with a bite spell (bite damage isn't dealt back).
- **Crossway Troublemakers:** their attacking Vampires get *deathtouch* (any damage kills) and *lifelink* (damage dealt gains them life).

### Sideboard: vs stronger opponents
Not for games against the Vampires deck, because these cards would tip the pair.
- **vs big creatures or bombs:** +2 Swords to Plowshares, +1 Stasis Snare, +1 Beast Within; −2 Rabid Bite, −1 Felling Blow, −1 Dryad Militant.
- **vs black decks:** +1 Knight of Grace (black removal can't target it); −1 Savannah Lions.
- **vs slow control decks:** +1 Harmonize (draw 3); −1 Broken Wings if they have no flyers.
- With the target list (no Dryad Militant or Savannah Lions), take out Helpful Hunter or a Carrot Cake instead.
- Don't overextend into a deck with board wipes: keep one or two creatures in hand.

### Head-to-head vs Orzhov Vampires (tested)

**Verdict: even**, about 51/49 Rabbits with both the owned lists and the lists with buys.

| Rabbits win % | Original simulator | Re-checked simulator |
|---|---|---|
| Owned vs owned | 50–51% | 52% |
| Both with buys | 51% | 51–52% |
| Rabbits with buys, Vampires owned | 60% | 60% |
| Rabbits owned, Vampires with buys | 42% | 45% |

**How it was tested.** A rules simulator played 8,000–10,000 games per matchup, alternating who goes first. An independent re-check reproduced the original results, then fixed six bugs and re-ran them. For example, both Harvestrite Hosts had shared one draw counter, and the attack AI undervalued going wide. What the simulator still leaves out roughly cancels: it has no double blocks and never casts Overrun unless it's lethal, which understates Rabbits, and it gives Vampires no instant-speed removal. Ten simulator games were also reviewed turn by turn (5–5), and 6 more were played by hand (3–3).

**Going first** wins about 53–54% of games.

#### Why it's even
- It's speed against staying power. Rabbits is faster and wider: it kills an empty board around turn 6, Vampires around turn 6.5. Vampires has more life, deathtouch blockers and reach (flyers and Exsanguinate).
- Rabbits has 5 removal spells (bite spells and Broken Wings, which need its own creatures). Vampires has 7.
- No single card is worth more than about 3 points, and neither main deck has a hoser or a one-sided sweeper.
- **Rabbits win** when Burrowguard Mentor or Druid of the Spade gets big alongside Treeguard Duo or an anthem before the removal lines up. **Vampires win** when Rabbits stumble on lands or colours, or when the Hinterland Sanctifier + Pridemate / Blight-Priest engine lands with removal behind it.

#### Buying rule
Each deck's buys are worth about 7–10 points, and upgrading only one deck tips the pair to 55–60%. Upgrade both together, in matched steps: Valley Questcallers with Vampire of the Dire Moons, Sunpetal Groves with Isolated Chapels, then Burrowguard Mentor, Harvestrite Hosts and Hop to It with Gifted Aetherborns and Vampire Nighthawk. On 2026-09-28 MTGMate had no Vampire of the Dire Moon, so hold the Questcallers until the Dire Moons are found. Keep both decks on their owned lists until both packages are complete, then swap them in on the same day.

#### Tuning levers (original simulator estimates)
- **If Rabbits win too often:** Rabbits' Regal Caracal → Pileated Provisioner (about −2), or, with the owned lists, Vampires' Kalastria Highborn → Pacifism or Knight of Malice from its sideboard (about +1 for Vampires).
- **If Vampires win too often:** Rabbits' Rabid Bite → Swords to Plowshares from its sideboard (about +3), or, with the owned lists, Dryad Militant → Stasis Snare (about +1).
- Keep Fumigate and Day of Judgment (free in the pool) out of both decks, because a one-sided sweeper would swing the pair.
- Tier-2 buys weren't simulated together. Buy them in matched pairs and re-check with a few games.

Simulator code and full game logs from the 2026-09-28 analysis are not kept in the repo.
